meta.name: Jay BIPU Content Idea Tournament
meta.pain_first_rule: An idea can only win by demonstrating the reader's pain more precisely than its opponent. Solution quality scores nothing until pain recognition scores.
meta.provenance: Pods seeded from Jay Yang's copywriting essay (docs/jay-yang-copywriting-article.md) and the live grader rubric.

pods.name: Time Poverty
pods.theme: The reader is drowning in work-on-the-business debt
ideas: You don't have a time problem, you have a key-man problem: everything routes to you because you never built a process that survives your absence.
The 60-hour week isn't ambition, it's an unpriced subsidy you're paying to avoid trusting anyone else with the important parts.
You didn't buy back your time when revenue grew — you just started renting it out to more customers at the same hourly rate.
Busy is not a growth stage. It's what stagnation looks like from inside while the calendar stays full.

pods.name: The Plateau
pods.theme: Revenue flatlined and nobody can name the constraint
ideas: Flat revenue for two quarters isn't a market condition. It's an unnamed bottleneck that everyone is quietly working around instead of naming.
You've optimized the wrong metric three quarters in a row because no one in the room will say which number actually gates growth.
Growth didn't stall. The thing that got you here ran out of runway, and 'work harder' was never the next lever.
Every business at $1-3M hits The Swamp: too busy to fix the business, too broke to hire the fix.

pods.name: Building Invisibly
pods.theme: Doing real work nobody sees, so nobody buys
ideas: Your product isn't underperforming. Your explanation of it loses to worse products with better sentences.
You're not being ignored because the market is noisy. You're invisible because you describe features while your buyer is scanning for their own pain in your first line.
Nobody repeats what you said because you gave them nothing pointable — no number, no logo, no receipt they could forward.
The best-kept secret in your industry is still a secret. Secrecy doesn't read as humility to a buyer; it reads as risk.

pods.name: The Trust Deficit
pods.theme: Audience likes the content but won't hand over money
ideas: Likes are not pre-orders. An audience that applauds but doesn't buy is telling you the proof layer is missing, not the promise.
They believe you're good. They don't believe you're good FOR THEM — proof that doesn't match the avatar reads as someone else's evidence.
'Trusted by industry leaders' converts nobody because trust needs a receipt, and adjectives aren't receipts.
You asked for the sale before you earned the belief. Belief without evidence is faith, and faith doesn't swipe a card.

pods.name: Someday Is A Plan
pods.theme: Reader keeps deferring the decision that would change things
ideas: The most dangerous line in your financial plan is the one that assumes your employer keeps paying you.
Cost of inaction compounds silently: every quarter on the current path prices you further out of the outcome you say you want.
There is no perfect time to start, only earlier and later — and later has a compounding interest rate you never see on the invoice.
Waiting for certainty is a decision too. It's the one where the window closes while you keep researching it.

judge_archetypes.name: The Skimmer
judge_archetypes.note: 3-second scroll test: only the first line and the felt punch register.

judge_archetypes.name: The Busy Operator
judge_archetypes.note: $1-3M owner skimming between meetings: does this name MY Tuesday afternoon?

judge_archetypes.name: The Skeptical Buyer
judge_archetypes.note: Wants receipts. Attacks unsupported claims. Rewards pointable evidence.

judge_archetypes.name: The Pattern Hunter
judge_archetypes.note: Rewards the Everyone-thinks-X / Problem-is-Y / Solution-is-Z structure.

judge_archetypes.name: The Tired Scroller
judge_archetypes.note: Reading at 3rd-grade level after a long day: anything requiring work is a loss.

format.round1: Within each pod, ideas face off pairwise; winners advance.
format.final: Pod champions meet in cross-pod bracket judged by all archetypes.
format.scoring: Each judge returns pain_recognition (0-5), specificity (0-5), action_pull (0-3). Pain recognition is weighted double and gates: if tied or losing on pain recognition, an idea cannot win regardless of other axes.
format.tiebreak: Higher pain_recognition, then higher specificity, then earlier seed order.
